questions.prompt: What does Vue Test Utils' mount() return?

options.text: A wrapper you can query, interact with, and inspect

questions.explanation: mount renders the component into a test DOM and returns a wrapper with methods like find, text, trigger, and emitted.

questions.prompt: Why should you await wrapper.trigger('click') before asserting on the result?

options.text: DOM updates are asynchronous, so awaiting ensures the DOM reflects the change before you assert

questions.explanation: Vue applies updates asynchronously; awaiting the triggered event (or nextTick) lets the DOM update before your assertion runs.

questions.prompt: How do you assert that a component emitted an event in a test?
questions.explanation: wrapper.emitted('eventName') returns the recorded emissions and their payloads, so you can assert the event fired with the right data.

questions.prompt: The fast, Vite-native test runner used for Vue unit tests is called ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: Vitest is a Vite-native test runner that shares your Vite config, so tests understand the same TypeScript and SFC setup.

questions.prompt: What should component tests primarily focus on?

options.text: Internal private refs and implementation details
User-visible behavior: rendered output, interactions, and emitted events
The exact number of lines of code

questions.explanation: Testing behavior (what the user sees and does, and what the component emits) keeps tests robust when you refactor internals.

questions.prompt: Order the typical Vite project workflow from start to shipping.
questions.explanation: Scaffold the project, develop with the dev server and HMR, produce a type-checked production build, then deploy the static dist/ files.
